## WordCraft: region names and the "Language (Region)" template

WordCraft builds a name such as "Spanish (Mexico)" from the translated language and the translated
region. The `{language} ({region})` template (only where a locale's brackets differ: `ja`, `ko`,
`zh-hans` and `zh-hant`) and the 69 region names (country or region, "U.A.E." to "South Africa") are
in `wordcraft.tsv` of every locale that has one. Contributor: Martin Ball with Claude Code (Claude
Sonnet 5.5), AI-assisted: written by the model from the plain meaning of the English, with no other
product's localisation consulted. **No native speaker has reviewed these rows.** Names are the
neutral, standard short forms; "Hong Kong SAR" and "Macao SAR" use each locale's word for special
administrative region.

## Language data

Every file under `language-data/` ([ADR 0004](docs/adr/0004-third-party-language-data.md),
[ADR 0005](docs/adr/0005-language-data-lives-here.md)), with its author, source, licence and
Licence class. Upstream files are kept unmodified. These rows moved here with the files from
WordCraft (`wordcraft@a88e00525`, `assets/hyphenation/` and `assets/spelling/`), byte for byte.
The checker (`crates/craft-i18n-tests/tests/language_data.rs`) fails when a file has no row or
more than one, a row has no file, the licence is empty or copyleft that can't be embedded (LGPL,
GPL, AGPL, CC-BY-SA), or the class isn't Embeddable. The licence table was signed off on
2026-11-01 ([ADR 0004](docs/adr/0004-third-party-language-data.md)). Language packs aren't
committed: `language-data/manifest.toml` records each pack file's source, licence and class
([format](docs/language-data-format.md)). `language-data/licences/<SPDX id>.txt` are the standard
licence texts from [spdx/license-list-data](https://github.com/spdx/license-list-data) @
`31846481de7ea17d92f2f46fad76abe58b2e9bb0`, copied verbatim as each licence permits.
